run.method: speech recovery game and assistive code-token adversary
run.brief: Create a valid schema_version 1 identity portfolio for run-19c-form-sound-code against atlas_version 1, using the method speech recovery game and assistive code-token adversary. The product is a pre-release Elixir/OTP library for declared, callable, measurable, and optimizable LM programs, with a credible artifact horizon spanning instructions, demonstrations, tool descriptions, retrieval policies, playbooks, schemas, code fragments, and configuration. It is not an official DSPy port, static proof system, universal agent OS, provider SDK, guaranteed autonomous self-improvement system, safety product, standards body, institute, or universal platform. Generate exactly 20 preserved candidates: 1-10 are sound-figures in abstract-sound-symbolic and play-games for international-users and elixir-newcomers, testing alliteration, rhyme, reduplication, ideophone, and onomatopoeia through speech recovery and plain phonetic guidance without imitating a regional sound to seem exotic; 11-20 are code-tokens in program-compilation and distributed-runtime for elixir-maintainers, beam-developers, and sre-platform, testing numerals, punctuation, operators, URI, and namespace systems with screen-reader-friendly spoken expansions and separately viable code projections. Include exactly four wildcards, two in each cell; sound stances 5 affirmative, 3 ambivalent, 2 adverse; code stances 5 affirmative, 2 ambivalent, 3 adverse; and per cell scopes 4 current, 4 horizon, 2 both. Every candidate needs non-null pronunciation and grammar, honest coined or no-source etymology, valid nonempty audience and architecture lenses, substantive rationale and concerns, and notes with challenge_wave, challenge_cell, form_mechanism, stance, scope, code_projection, current_embodiment, and horizon_embodiment. Code projections must give viable hex, otp, module, mix, config, and telemetry forms, and symbolic identities must not claim a protocol or standard role.
